functionalObligations.text: a qualified purchaser subscribes and receives a share in a British Virgin Islands limited company, recorded on chain as a six-decimal token
functionalObligations.note: Sworn on Form D/A filed 2026-07-27: BVI, incorporated 2023, exemptions 06c plus 3C plus 3C.7, is40Act false, placement agent Securitize Markets LLC (CRD 283256), cumulative totalAmountSold $5,135,523,412 across 28 recorded investors, first sale 2024-03-04. Live on Ethereum: Class A 0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec, name BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund, totalSupply 224,848,357.43, walletCount 59; Class I 0x6a9da2d710bb9b700acde7cb81f10f1ff8c89041, supply 964,123,531.86. THREE FIGURES, THREE MEANINGS: totalIssued on Class A is 2,254,889,229.88 (cumulative gross issuance), and no single number is BUIDL's AUM without naming which chain, which class, and whether the figure is outstanding or cumulative.

functionalObligations.text: the fund targets a constant one-dollar share value with no price feed of any kind on chain, warns in the same sentence that it may fail, and disclaims any sponsor obligation to support it
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and it is worth stating positively rather than as an omission. Ex is CORRECTLY ABSENT: there is no oracle, no price contract, no latestRoundData, and BUIDL is the only member of the five with no price source of any kind, because the unit is assumed at par and yield arrives as supply. The disclaimer is verbatim: you could lose money by investing in the Fund; although the Fund seeks to preserve the value of your investment at $1.00 per share, it cannot guarantee it will do so; the Fund's sponsor has no legal obligation to provide financial support to the Fund. Nothing in the vocabulary names a targeted-but-unguaranteed par value, which is the entire economic proposition of a money-market fund.

functionalObligations.text: yield is declared off chain against a snapshot of who held the token at three in the afternoon eastern time, and paid the following business day by minting new tokens to them
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Verbatim: dividends are accrued each calendar day to the holder of record at 3:00pm ET, and paid out the following business day in the form of new BUIDL tokens. CORRECTION to the corpus, which records this as monthly; it is DAILY accrual paid next business day. Four symbols were considered and each fails for a stated reason. Not Ix: there is no index and the unit stays at one dollar. Not Rb: balances change by a discrete issuance event, not by a global scaling factor. Not Sh alone: the pro-rata claim per token is constant and what varies is how many tokens you are given. Not Ep: the 3pm instant is a wall-clock snapshot taken by an off-chain administrator, not an on-chain period boundary that gates a transition. A discretionary dividend declared off-chain against a holder-of-record snapshot and settled in kind by minting has no symbol.

functionalObligations.text: the token may only move between investors an off-chain onboarding process has whitelisted, checked on every transfer by an on-chain compliance service
functionalObligations.note: BUIDL adheres to high KYC/AML standards and only permits token transfers to whitelisted investors. Verified rather than asserted: the deployed contract responds to getDSService(uint256), totalIssued(), walletCount() and isPaused(), and the service IDs returned match the DS Protocol constants TRUST_SERVICE 1, REGISTRY_SERVICE 4, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE 8 read from the interface source. Live services: Trust 0x3a68756d0335e75c909ba1e8fefc1d4832c36c60, Registry 0x0dac900f26de70336f2320f7ccedee70ff6a1a5b, Compliance 0x07a1ebfb9a9a421249ddc71bddb8860cc077e3a9. Every transfer runs preTransferCheck(address,address,uint) against the compliance service, so L16 (transfer-time enforcement) is discharged.

functionalObligations.text: the on-chain ledger is keyed on a legal identity rather than on an address: wallets are attached to an investor identifier, and the investor carries attributes that expire and that point at an off-chain document
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. balanceOfInvestor(string _id), registerInvestor(string,string), addWallet(address,string), setCountry(string,string), and setAttribute(string _id, uint8 _attributeId, uint256 _value, uint256 _expiry, string _proofHash) with constants KYC_APPROVED 1, ACCREDITED 2, QUALIFIED 4, PROFESSIONAL 8. Aw is a bit; this is a subsystem with its own key space, its own time dimension and its own pointer into a legal file. An attribute that EXPIRES means eligibility decays with no actor doing anything. It also means the chain is not a bearer ledger even in form, which is the on-chain half of the register-of-record finding at F10.

functionalObligations.text: the gate tests two distinct legal predicates at once, accredited-investor status under the securities law and qualified-purchaser status under the investment-company law, and the tighter of the two is what caps the fund's investor base
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The Form D's federalExemptionsExclusions are exactly 06c, 3C and 3C.7, and the product page corroborates with Investor Eligibility: Qualified Purchaser. Aw names the gate and never what it is testing for. It cannot distinguish a gate that exists to satisfy a resale restriction from one that exists to preserve a fund's exemption from registration, and THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY AND THE REMEDIES DIFFER. Regulation S is NOT evidenced and is marked UNKNOWN rather than refuted, because Reg S offerings are not reported on Form D.

functionalObligations.text: the issuer can take tokens from one holder and give them to another, recording a reason string on chain, and can burn them
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fz), and the only member of the five with a real seize. seize(address _from, address _to, uint256 _value, string _reason), burn(address,uint256,string _reason), issueTokens(address,uint256) and issueTokensCustom with a lock and a _releaseTime, all onlyIssuerOrAbove. RESIDUE INSIDE THE SYMBOL: Fz reads as an emergency lever, and here forced transfer is ROUTINE TRANSFER-AGENT ADMINISTRATION, the on-chain expression of remedies a registrar already has for lost certificates, court orders and escheatment. L28 (named authority, enumerated triggers, appeal path, holder disclosure) is partially discharged only, because the reason string is free text and no trigger list is published. Provenance caveat: these are the PUBLISHED INTERFACES (Solidity 0.4.23) and the deployed implementation records solc 0.8.13, so conformance is established by calling the contract and provenance is not.

functionalObligations.text: an issuer-level role can halt the token entirely
functionalObligations.note: Live isPaused() returns false on the Class A token (JSON-RPC eth.llamarpc.com and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, accessed 2026-08-04). Gp names the facility; who holds it is F13.

functionalObligations.text: a holder may redeem for cash on the same business day if the request reaches the transfer agent in good order between eight in the morning and three in the afternoon eastern time on a redemption date
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and the corpus marker stands: this is a subscription-document right against a BVI company exercisable on a business-day calendar, not a redemption the contract can honour. There is no on-chain redemption function that pays anything; the on-chain leg is a transfer to the transfer agent's wallet and the cash leg is banking. Ep was considered for the cut-off and REJECTED under the rule applied across this lane, that an off-chain banking calendar is not an on-chain epoch. UNKNOWN: BUIDL's authoritative subscription calendar; the monthly-close table on the platform page carries a Luxembourg-time reference and reads as a shared Securitize template rather than as BUIDL's own terms. The Form D swears a minimum of $100,000 while the product page advertises $5M with $250k subsequent for the Ethereum class; both are primary and both are reported.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know whether the chain is the register of ownership or a mirror of a transfer agent's book, and here a redemption completed on chain before the deadline is not a redemption: if the transfer agent has not yet determined the transfer to be final and recorded it in the fund's books, the shares are not redeemed that day and roll to the next redemption date
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and it is the single most important structural fact about BUIDL and the strongest sentence found anywhere in this category. Verbatim: redemptions of Shares effected on the blockchain at or immediately prior to the redemption deadline on a Redemption Date may not be recorded on the Fund's books and records prior to such deadline, including if the Transfer Agent has not yet determined that the transfer of Shares to its wallet is final; in such event, the Shares will not be redeemed on such Redemption Date; rather they will be redeemed on the next Redemption Date. The fund's books and records are a DISTINCT ARTEFACT from the blockchain and are AUTHORITATIVE OVER IT: the chain is an instruction channel the transfer agent reads, and the register is a separate book the transfer agent writes. Sv was considered for the transfer agent's determination and REJECTED: Sv names discretion over how an obligation is serviced or valued, not discretion over WHETHER AN EXECUTED ON-CHAIN TRANSFER EXISTS. Nothing in the 58 can say that a settled state transition may be treated as not having happened.

functionalObligations.text: the registrar of that authoritative book is a distinct SEC-registered entity from the broker-dealer that sells the fund, and it outsources its own recordkeeping to a legacy stock transfer agent
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION: the corpus names the wrong company. The SEC-registered transfer agent is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC, CIK 0001782266, TA file 084-06638, FINS 003641, TA-1/A filed 2025-12-30 from Miami, named Securitize LLC until 2025-04-14, sole member Securitize Inc., CEO Carlos Domingo. Securitize Markets, LLC is the BROKER-DEALER and placement agent (CRD 283256) and appears on the Form D as receiving sales compensation. Two companies, two registrations. Its own TA-1 declares an engaged service company in both directions, Pacific Stock Transfer (084-01145, Las Vegas), so the chain of custody of the authoritative record runs token to Securitize to a legacy Nevada transfer agent. Nothing in the vocabulary reaches one link of that chain, let alone three. The corpus's SUBSTANTIVE claim, that the transfer agent's book is the legal register and the token is a mirror, is confirmed and strengthened; only the entity name was wrong.

functionalObligations.text: the implementation behind the token can be replaced in one call, on a hand-rolled proxy that exposes nothing but an owner and a target
functionalObligations.note: Measured, not asserted. The Class A token 0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec is a 703-byte hand-rolled delegatecall proxy, NOT EIP-1967. Its runtime exposes exactly four functions, owner() 0x8da5cb5b, target() 0xd4b83992, setOwner(address) 0x13af4035 and setTarget(address) 0x776d1a01, with storage slot 0 the owner and slot 1 the implementation, and a fallback that delegatecalls to slot 1. Live target() = 0x603bb6909be14f83282e03632280d91be7fb83b2 (17,236 bytes). The I-Class token is a standard EIP-1967 proxy with implementation 0x9e2693f54831f6f52b0bb952c2935d26919a3626. Read by direct JSON-RPC against eth.llamarpc.com and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com on 2026-08-04. Up names the facility and stops there; F13 is what the facility is worth.

functionalObligations.text: the party who holds that replacement power is one private key: the proxy owner is an externally owned account, with no multisig at the proxy layer and no delay of any kind
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and this is the finding the corpus's decomposition failed to record. owner() on the Class A proxy is 0xe01605f6b6dc593b7d2917f4a0940db2a625b09e, which returns eth_getCode = 0x and nonce 10 on two independent RPC endpoints, so it is an externally owned account, not a contract; the I-Class proxy has the SAME EOA owner. One private key can call setTarget and replace the entire implementation of a multi-hundred-million-dollar BlackRock fund token, immediately. THIS ARMS PROHIBITION X9 (Up with immediate single-key control, class H), and the corpus records armedProhibitions as empty for BUIDL, so this is a finding about the decomposition process rather than about the vocabulary. It is stated here as an obligation ABOUT THE HOLDER rather than about the facility because that is exactly what the vocabulary cannot carry: Up says a mutable implementation exists, and it cannot express who may mutate it, how fast, or with what independence. Tg is correctly absent and its absence is not neutrality but the alarming case: there is no timelock because there is no governance, only a key. This is the same party-sort gap the 07-bridges lane exhibited on the three largest wrapped-asset bridges. L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is NOT discharged.

functionalObligations.text: the same fund issues a legally distinct share class on each chain, priced with a different management fee, against one off-chain register, and movement between chains is a third-party service the fund disclaims
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE that REVERSES a corpus attribution. Xf and Xm are REFUTED as BUIDL's own mechanisms and are dropped from the construction. Ethereum, Arbitrum and Optimism carry 50 bps; Aptos, Avalanche, Polygon and Solana carry 20 bps. Verbatim: bridging is provided by a 3rd party provider and availability cannot be guaranteed at all times or between all blockchains. If Xm belongs to anything it belongs to Wormhole, and Xf describes a facility the fund disclaims. There is no symbol for ONE OBLIGOR, N TOKENS, ONE REGISTER, which is a different object from a claim moved between domains. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CORPUS: identicalClaimedByLane records USYC and BUIDL as identical; they are not, they differ by at least four symbols as the corpus itself writes them, and the cross-domain attribution between the two is REVERSED, since USYC is natively issued on three chains with dedicated cross-chain tellers while BUIDL disclaims bridging entirely.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know who owes them the money and what recourse they have, and here the obligor is a BVI company whose sponsor has expressly disclaimed any obligation to support it and whose gating powers are unknowable
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Obligor: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd., a BVI limited company incorporated 2023, registered office care of 50 Hudson Yards, New York, relying on 3(c)(7) and 506(c), board on the current filing Ian Pilgrim (Bermuda), W. William Woods (Cayman), Noelle L'Heureux (San Francisco) and Jennifer Collins (Carne Group, Cayman). Recourse: the sponsor has no legal obligation to provide financial support at any time, so a holder's remedy is a claim against the BVI company under private subscription documents. UNKNOWN: the board's suspension or gating power. The fund is not an EDGAR reporting company and files only Form D, and the subscription documents are not public, so no gate may be asserted in either direction. No element of the 58 names an obligor, a recourse position, or a suspension power.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know whether their claim survives the fund's insolvency, and here it is unsecured equity: no security interest, no collateral agent, no bankruptcy-remoteness claim and no perfection step anywhere
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the contrast within the category is the point. Ondo asserts a first-priority perfected security interest with a named collateral agent and control agreements; BUIDL asserts nothing of the kind, because a share is not a secured claim. Nothing on the product page, in the Form D, or in the DS Protocol interfaces creates or perfects any security interest, and no non-consolidation or true-sale opinion is referenced. A BUIDL holder ranks behind the fund's creditors, and no on-chain artefact records that, tests it, or changes on it. Of the five products in this category exactly one claims perfection, and the vocabulary cannot state the difference between the two positions.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know what the reserve holds and who custodies it, and here the only public statement of the portfolio is a marketing phrase and the custodian could not be established at a primary source
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The whole of the public portfolio policy is core investments of overnight repo and 3-month Treasuries. UNKNOWN: BNY Mellon's role split between fund administrator, custodian and digital-asset custody could not be confirmed at a primary source; the product page's institutional-grade custody section did not render entity names on scrape and press assertions are Tier 4 and are declined. The corpus's claim that the custodian's failure is the dominant tail risk and is unnameable is probably right, but the custodian's identity is not established here and must not be asserted.

functionalObligations.text: no independent attestation of the fund's assets is published anywhere obtainable: there is no holdings feed, no reserve report, no oracle and no covenant
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: At is DROPPED from the corpus construction for BUIDL. The corpus emits At and stage 1 found no evidence for it. L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse, and not one of the five is evidenced for BUIDL, so At cannot be discharged at all rather than being merely approximate. This makes BUIDL the largest fund in the category with the smallest construction, six symbols, all of them access-control, freeze, redemption, share accounting and upgradeability, which is precisely the corpus's own category verdict that the vocabulary's RWA coverage is an access-control and upgrade-authority coverage.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know who may change what the money is invested in, and here the manager can change duration, issuer mix and repo exposure at will with nothing on chain constraining it
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirmed as unnameable. Nothing on chain constrains duration, issuer mix or repo exposure; there is no oracle, no holdings feed and no covenant, so the manager can change the entire risk profile of the instrument without touching a contract and no element in the vocabulary is sensitive to that. Sv is not emitted anywhere in this spec: BUIDL has no on-chain determination for Sv to attach to, since there is no price to set and no loss to mark, so investment discretion here is residue in the purest form of the five.
